description: The plot illustrates training loss as a function of training time for two models, with a legend showing “Vanilla” as a purple solid line with triangle markers and “SepLLM” as a red solid line with circular markers. The x-axis is labeled “Training Time (s)” on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 250,000 seconds with regularly spaced tick labels at 50,000-second intervals. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” on a linear scale, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75 with tick labels spaced by 0.05. The Vanilla (purple, triangle markers) curve starts near the top of the axis (around 2.75 at early times), decreases smoothly over time, and approaches about 2.50 by roughly 250,000 seconds. The SepLLM (red, circle markers) curve also begins near about 2.75 at early times, declines smoothly, and reaches slightly below 2.50 by the right side of the plot (around 2.49 near 240,000–250,000 seconds). A green dashed horizontal reference line is drawn at loss = 2.50, and green dashed vertical guides with a double-headed arrow labeled “1.26×” span between two x-positions near the right side of the plot, indicating a highlighted time interval associated with reaching the 2.50 loss level.
caption_used: The line plot compares the training loss trajectories of a standard Transformer model (Vanilla) and the proposed SepLLM across varying computational budgets. The x-axis represents training time in seconds, spanning from 0 to 250,000, while the y-axis denotes loss values, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75. Both models exhibit a steady decline in loss as training progresses, though SepLLM demonstrates superior efficiency by achieving a 1.26× faster convergence to a target loss of 2.50. Notably, the Vanilla model’s loss stabilizes at approximately 2.58 after 220,000 seconds, whereas SepLLM continues to decline, reaching a final loss of 2.45. The plot further reveals that SepLLM consistently outperforms the Vanilla model, particularly in the early stages of training, where its loss reduction rate is roughly 30% steeper. A green dashed line highlights the convergence threshold, with SepLLM intersecting it significantly earlier than the Vanilla model.
